input.quote: HDI agrees that it shall promote the Site and Deerskin Products no less favorably than it promotes HDI's
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no most-favoured-nation obligation on the Company. A full read of the fee, exclusivity, cross-promotion and general provisions (§§ 3, 6, 7, 10) shows no requirement that the Company extend HDI its best terms, match third-party offers, or grant HDI terms no less favourable than those given to others. The only "no less favorably" undertaking (§ 1.8, p0013) runs in our favour: HDI must promote the Site and Deerskin Products no less favourably than its own catalog titles. The § 7.1 cross-promotion covenant is a mutual "reciprocal and equitable basis" commitment rather than a favoured-terms obligation, and § 6.1 exclusivity is a separate commercial term addressed under the exclusivity rule. This meets the preferred position (no MFN burdening the Customer, favoured treatment running to us), so no redline is proposed.
